solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Holy man, a theologian observed in close briefly

indicators.note: something said briefly is cut short, so the word loses its final letter
to be seen in a place is to sit within it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: to close a door is to shut it; trimmed to SHU
taken as written
DD is a Doctor of Divinity

explanation.surface: A holy man and a scholar of religion are spotted somewhere nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' looks like an adjective meaning near, but it is the verb shut, docked to SHU, and A DD sits inside it to make SADDHU.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadhu or saddhu is a Hindu ascetic who has renounced worldly life, a wandering religious figure.

clue.text: Ship leaking a bit apparently? Tools required

blocks.note: the S of SS, a steamship
a slow leak dribbles out, one drop at a time

explanation.surface: A slightly leaky vessel needs some tools to fix it.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'S trickles', a ship leaking a bit; 'apparently' flags that split. The word is obscure, so the wordplay does the work.
explanation.definitionFit: A strickle is a straight-edged implement used for levelling grain in a measure, shaping moulds or sharpening scythes.

clue.text: Be different, putting girl on edge

blocks.note: Di, short for Diana, a stock crossword girl
a verge is a border or edge, as of a road

explanation.surface: Someone stands out from the crowd by making a young woman nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On edge' reads as nervous, but in a down clue 'on' puts the girl on top of the edge word.
explanation.definitionFit: When opinions or paths diverge they separate and go different ways, so to diverge is to differ.

clue.text: Like some drinks offering cure when brother’s upset inside

indicators.note: to upset something is to knock it over, and in a down clue that turns it upside down
a word placed inside sits within the other word

blocks.note: to cure is to heal
BR is the abbreviation for brother

explanation.surface: A drink promises to cure you when your brother is feeling sick inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset inside' reads like an upset stomach, but 'upset' turns the brother upside down, as it can in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbal teas and infusions are made from plants, so some drinks are described with this adjective.

clue.text: Fever? Spirit must be knocked back with water

indicators.note: a drink knocked back is downed, but read literally the word is sent backwards

blocks.note: rum is a spirit
rain is water from the sky

explanation.surface: A cure for fever: knock back a spirit with water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' suggests drinking the spirit; instead it reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Murrain is an old name for infectious disease in cattle, including feverish plagues, so the question mark hedges the example.

clue.text: Join together in old-fashioned expression of surprise

blocks.note: first meaning: unite in wedlock
second meaning: an archaic exclamation, originally an oath by the Virgin Mary

explanation.surface: A couple are wed amid gasps of old-time astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marry!' is the Shakespearean exclamation, from 'by Mary', still met in historical dialogue.
explanation.definitionFit: Marrying unites two people as a couple, and the archaic interjection voiced surprise or indignation.

clue.text: Teacher and old-fashioned rocker chatted

blocks.note: a rabbi is a Jewish teacher of the law
a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British rock-and-roll fan

explanation.surface: A teacher and an ageing rock fan had a natter.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style suits who loved rock and roll. To rabbit, from rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork' for talk, is British for chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to rabbit on is to talk at length, so rabbited is past tense for chattered away.

clue.text: Rubbish mostly hidden under a sea mollusc

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: taken as written
baloney is nonsense; docked to BALONE

explanation.surface: Litter lies under the waves, concealing a shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A sea' looks like one unit, but only A is wordplay; 'sea' belongs to the definition. In a down clue 'hidden under' puts the rubbish beneath the A.
explanation.definitionFit: The abalone is an edible marine snail with an ear-shaped shell lined with mother-of-pearl.

clue.text: Enid’s boy with absence of daddy regularly missing out

indicators.note: skipping at regular intervals drops every other letter

blocks.note: no means none, an absence
the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A woman's son grows up with his father missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Enid is Enid Blyton, the British children's author whose little wooden boy lives in Toyland.
explanation.definitionFit: Noddy is the nodding-headed toy character created by the children's writer Enid Blyton in 1949.

clue.text: Enthusiastic fans, maybe, about to meet Queen in county

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: C for circa, Latin for about
Hants is the abbreviation for Hampshire, an English county
ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Devoted supporters are about to meet the Queen on a royal visit to the shires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'soon going to'; here 'about' gives C and 'to meet' just joins it on. Hants is the standard short form of Hampshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Football crowds and other keen supporters sing and shout slogans in unison, so they are chanters by example.

clue.text: Partygoer in posh car straddling half of road

indicators.note: taking half keeps only part of the word and drops the rest
to straddle is to sit astride, with one part on each side of another

blocks.note: RR is a Rolls-Royce
an avenue is a road; its first half is AVE

explanation.surface: A reveller is in a luxury car parked across the middle of the street.
explanation.walkthrough: The posh car is the Rolls-Royce, abbreviated to its two initials, and 'half' takes the first three of six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A raver is someone who goes to raves or wild parties, a lively party-lover in colloquial speech.

clue.text: Directors faced with difficult sort of material

blocks.note: difficult means hard
a company's directors form its board

explanation.surface: The board of directors has to deal with a troublesome kind of person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faced with' puts the second word in front of the first, so the directors come after 'difficult'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardboard is stiff sheet building material made from compressed wood fibres, used for panels and backing.

clue.text: Church really gutted about blemish — that’s inevitable

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for a noun: something that's inevitable

indicators.note: gutting removes the insides, leaving only the outer letters
to go about something is to surround it

blocks.note: CE, Church of England
only the first and last letters survive
a taint is a stain or blemish

explanation.surface: A church is devastated by a scandal, and nothing can be done about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutted' reads as British slang for bitterly disappointed, but it empties the word, leaving R and Y around the blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: A certainty is something bound to happen, a sure thing, so it is whatever is inevitable.

clue.text: Plant with interior that’s yellow and off-white

indicators.note: an interior is what lies inside, so one piece is set within the other

blocks.note: ivy is a climbing plant
or is gold or yellow in heraldry

explanation.surface: A flower whose centre is yellow and whose petals are cream.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic word for gold or yellow, a regular in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivory is the creamy colour of elephant tusk, a pale shade just short of pure white.

clue.text: Heartless biographies — don’t believe them!

definitions.note: the pronoun stands for the plural noun

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letter is taken out

blocks.note: biographies are Lives, as in Lives of the Saints

explanation.surface: A warning against unfeeling biographies that trash their subjects.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle V goes from the five-letter word for biographies.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsehoods are things one should not trust, so the imperative describes untruths in a roundabout way.

clue.text: Making sure priest and soldiers can be accommodated in group

indicators.note: to be accommodated is to be housed inside, so pieces go within another

blocks.note: a curé is a French parish priest
soldiers are men, the other ranks
a set is a group

explanation.surface: Checking that a clergyman and troops will fit in with the party.
explanation.walkthrough: The priest and soldiers together sit inside SET.
explanation.definitionFit: Securement is the act of securing, making something safe or certain, so it names the action of guaranteeing.

clue.text: Wearing special clothes not fashionable, lacking shape

indicators.note: not means without, so the following word is taken away

blocks.note: wearing a uniform
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Someone in costume but out of fashion looks shapeless.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is flawed, as the Times blog noted: removing IN from UNIFORMED leaves UFORMED, and only dropping the I gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unformed has not yet taken a definite shape or structure, so it is shapeless.

clue.text: Politician falling short with adviser a cruel person

indicators.note: falling short means not quite reaching the end, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: a Tory is a British Conservative; docked to TOR
a mentor is a trusted adviser

explanation.surface: A disappointing politician and his adviser are a nasty piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who inflicts suffering on others deliberately is cruel, which is what a tormentor does.

clue.text: Without means to pay, is in Paris for medical check

blocks.note: skint is British slang for penniless
est is French for is

explanation.surface: Broke in Paris and in need of seeing a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: Skint is British slang for having no money; 'in Paris' asks for the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: A skin test applies an allergen or agent to the skin to diagnose allergy or infection, a medical examination.

clue.text: Removes message implying workers will go back to work

definitions.text: message implying workers will go back to work

blocks.note: first meaning: deletes from a list or register

blocks.clueFragment: message implying workers will go back to work
blocks.note: second meaning: a terse announcement that industrial action is cancelled

explanation.surface: A notice that the walkout is over and staff are returning.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the phrase as 'strike's off', the stoppage called off.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike off is to erase a name from a roll, as a doctor or lawyer is struck off for misconduct.

clue.text: Rebuke agent wanting to go hither and thither

blocks.note: a rep is a sales representative, an agent
to wander aimlessly

explanation.surface: A boss tells off a sales agent who keeps wandering about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting to' only joins; the agent is followed by a word for wandering.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprove someone is to scold or criticise them for a fault, a close synonym of rebuke.

clue.text: Square where two answers start in this puzzle

definitions.text: where two answers start in this puzzle

blocks.note: first meaning: a square number, two times two

blocks.clueFragment: where two answers start in this puzzle
blocks.note: second meaning: the grid number shared by an across and a down entry

explanation.walkthrough: 'Square' looks like a grid cell, which fits the second half, but it means a number that is a perfect square; 4-across and 4-down both begin at that numbered cell.
explanation.definitionFit: Two multiplied by itself makes this number, and in this grid it labels the cell starting MURRAIN and MARRY.

clue.text: No let-up working if you want to get rich

indicators.note: something working is in operation, moving about, so the letters are set in motion

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice that constant graft is the way to become wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' seems part of the work-ethic sentiment; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent describes great wealth and lavish luxury, so it is a synonym for being wealthy.

clue.text: Furthest point attained by wild animal I caught climbing

indicators.note: climbing goes upward, and in a down clue that runs the letters backwards
something caught is held within a grip, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: an ape is an animal of the wild
ego is Latin for I, the self

explanation.surface: An animal scales the heights and reaches the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' is not a letter here but the self, the ego.
explanation.definitionFit: The apogee is the point in an orbit furthest from the earth, and by extension a peak or climax.

clue.text: Recognised player regularly taking food provided by poulterer

blocks.note: a player selected for a national team is awarded a cap
someone on a medicine takes it regularly

explanation.surface: An international sportsman stocks up on food bought from the poultry shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' looks like a signal to take alternate letters, but it goes with 'taking': to be on a drug is to take it regularly.
explanation.definitionFit: A capon is a castrated cockerel fattened for the table, sold by a dealer in poultry.

clue.text: Source of oil artist needs to acquire first

blocks.note: to cop is informal for to get or catch
RA, Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A painter must buy their oil paint before starting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oil' suggests the painter's medium; 'first' puts the acquiring word before the artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Copra is the dried kernel of the coconut, from which coconut oil is pressed.

clue.text: Special writing with fancy pictures enthralling toddler ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is taken
fancy means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters are rearranged
to enthral is to hold captive, so one piece is held inside

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter

explanation.surface: An illustrated book whose pictures captivate a small child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy pictures' reads as ornate illustrations, but 'fancy' shuffles the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Scripture is sacred writing such as the Bible, set apart from ordinary texts.

clue.text: Leader of subversives put down, killed

indicators.note: the leader is the one at the front, so the first letter is taken

blocks.note: the opening letter
past participle of lay down, set down

explanation.surface: The rebel chief has been crushed and executed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put down' reads as suppressed or killed, but here it is lain, as in lying down.
explanation.definitionFit: Slain is the past participle of slay, a literary verb meaning to kill violently.

clue.text: Walk quietly and meanderingly round capital, ending in cafe

indicators.note: meandering winds about, so the letters take a winding new order
the ending of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: p, piano, is quiet in music
Rome, capital of Italy
taken as written
its last letter

explanation.surface: A tourist strolls idly around a city before finishing up at a café.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital is Rome; the blog reads NAD as the jumbled 'and' following it.
explanation.definitionFit: A promenade is a leisurely stroll, typically in public, so it is a kind of walk.

clue.text: Man hugging wife somewhere in Wales once

indicators.note: a hug wraps arms around someone, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: a gent is a gentleman
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A husband embraces his wife on a trip to Wales long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' matters: Gwent was a Welsh county from 1974 to 1996.
explanation.definitionFit: Gwent was a former administrative county of south-east Wales, abolished in 1996, so it was a place in Wales formerly.

clue.text: Savant troubled about English language that’s passed out of use

definitions.text: language that’s passed out of use

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters are thrown out of order
to be about something is to go around it

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A scholar frets over English as a dying tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Savant' looks like the scholar who studies the language, but its letters are the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Avestan is the ancient Iranian language of the Zoroastrian scriptures, long extinct as a spoken tongue.

clue.text: Put off when receiving mark of wrong or right

indicators.note: receiving means taking something in, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: to deter is to discourage
a cross marks a wrong answer

explanation.surface: Someone is discouraged when their work comes back marked right or wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or' looks like part of 'wrong or right', but it only joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dexter is Latin for right-hand side and survives in heraldry for the right side of a shield.
